title: POC benchmarking & acceptance plan for Modulex Analytics
text:
POC benchmarking & acceptance plan for Modulex Analytics

['From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Ayesha Khan <ayesha.khan@modulex.ai>, Rafael Ortiz <rafael.ortiz@modulex.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-08-28T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: POC benchmarking & acceptance plan for Modulex Analytics

Hi Ayesha / Rafael —

Thanks again for the demo and the deep dive this morning. Quick recap and my proposal for a tightly-scoped POC so we can validate performance, cost, and quality against your user workload. Below is what we discussed and a recommended acceptance plan.

High-level POC structure (6 weeks total)
- Week 0: Kickoff & data ingest (security review, sample dataset delivery)
- Weeks 1–2: Smoke benchmarks (latency baseline, correctness on a 1k example set)
- Weeks 3–4: Scale testing (throughput runs, concurrency/peak scenarios)
- Weeks 5–6: Validation & handover (quality review, cost/ops recommendations)

Success criteria (proposal — happy to iterate)
- Latency: p95 generation latency <= 250 ms for 512-token prompts (target 200 ms)
- Throughput: sustain 400–600 QPS for short-form inference windows during peak sim
- Cost: target < $0.06 per 1k tokens at POC scale, with breakouts by model variant and batching
- Quality: human eval accuracy >= 85% on your labeled 500-sample set (or equivalent QA metric); automated unit tests pass >= 95%

Technical approach / experiments
1) Baseline run (no caching, single-request latency profile)
2) Caching + optimized batching (expect 20–40% token-cost reduction)
3) Quantization + runtime kernel selection (we’ll compare q4 vs q8 variants)

Owners / asks
- Modulex: provide sample traffic CSV (anonymized) + 500 labeled QA samples; identify SRE contact for network/firewall testing.
- Redwood: deliver test harness, run benchmark matrix (attached), share results and a short ops README.
- Internal owners: Karthik (tech lead for benchmark runs), Mina (infrastructure / infra setup), Ben & Monica (CS + success measurements).

Attachments: moduplex-sample-traffic.csv, moduplex-benchmark-specs.xlsx (attached).
Next steps
- Ayesha: confirm sample dataset delivery date (proposed by 2025-09-01).
- Redwood: share DocuSign MOU for POC and a kickoff calendar invite — I’ll send both today.

If this looks good I’ll schedule a 30-min kickoff next week and Karthik will walk through the technical runbook.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0124

Thanks Sean — this is very clear and helpful. A few quick clarifications from our side before we sign off the MOU: 

1) Data/security: our security team requires SOC 2 evidence and confirmation of dataset retention rules. Will Redwood sign the standard data handling addendum?
2) Cost estimate: can you provide a rough not-to-exceed estimate for the 6-week POC (just ballpark) so I can get budgetary approval?
3) Model variants: we prefer to test the 13B and a 7B variant. Are those options in your hosted fleet or would we run dedicated?

We aim to deliver an anonymized sample dataset by 2025-09-01; Rafael will coordinate with our SRE to open a temporary VPN if needed.

Ayesha

Subject: Re: POC benchmarking & acceptance plan for Modulex Analytics

Hi Ayesha — quick tech follow-up to make sure the runs reflect your production profile: 

- Please confirm typical prompt and completion lengths (median / 90th percentile token counts). If you don’t have labeled stats, a representative sample of 5–10 sessions is fine.
- Concurrency: is the 400–600 QPS estimate intended as concurrent short requests (1–3 calls/session) or batched multi-turn flows?
- Model choices: we can run Llama-2-13B (q8/q4 variants) and a tuned 7B. Hosted fleet can support both for smoke; for sustained peak testing we recommend Redwood Dedicated or a short-term dedicated pool to avoid noisy neighbors — I’ll include both result types in the report.
- Quantization: are you OK with us using q4 quantized runtimes for cost testing? We’ll log fidelity regressions per experiment.

Planned experiments (brief)
A) Latency profile (single-worker, no cache) — p50/p95/p99
B) Throughput stress (gradually increase concurrency to target QPS; measure tail latency)
C) Cost sweep (batch sizes, quantization variants, caching on/off)

Operational asks for initial setup
- Modulex: deliver anonymized CSV + a small API key/test account (limited scope) or allow us to replay traffic from the CSV.
- Redwood: Mina will provision the test harness and a telemetry dashboard; Monica will run quality validation with your labeled set.

I’ll draft the exact benchmark commands and expected metrics in the shared Drive (link above) later today.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

Ayesha / Rafael —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Per the questions above, here’s a concise mutual action plan to move to kickoff: 

Mutual Action Plan (kickoff -> handover)
- Redwood to send MOU (DocuSign) with standard DPA and SOC2 reference — today (Sean) — link: https://app.docusign.com/MOU-Redwood-Modulex-2025
- Modulex to deliver anonymized sample CSV + 500 labeled QA samples — target 2025-09-01 (Ayesha / Rafael)
- Redwood to provision test harness + baseline run results (Karthik / Mina) — baseline results by 2025-09-08
- Cost snapshot and ops playbook (Redwood) — deliver by 2025-09-15 (Monica)
- Final validation review & go/no-go (joint) — week of 2025-09-22

Notes: for the long-run throughput tests we recommend a short Dedicated slot to ensure consistent tail latency; we’ll include both dedicated and hosted comparisons in the cost report. If Modulex prefers, we can scope the Dedicated quote as a separate optional line in the MOU.

I’ll send a calendar invite for a 30-min kickoff (proposed: 2025-09-02 at 10:00 AM PT). Rafael — can you confirm SRE availability to open the VPN/test endpoints that week?

Thanks — looking forward to getting started.

Sean Gallagher
